reviews.title: So close to 5 stars!
reviews.text: I really want to give this app five stars and if all you care about are calories and a couple of very basic macros like protein then it’s a five star app. For me, and for a ton of people, what would elevate this, and quite easily, would be to allow us to track sodium on this app. It’s so close to perfect, but this obvious and persistent flaw remains over years of requests to the developer.

reviews.title: Quantity button does not work
reviews.text: Great app except all of a sudden the quantity button doesn’t work properly for days now and I can’t find where to contact support to address the issue. It’s driving me nuts now and I’m ready to quit. This is after I’ve recommended the app and my family is also on it. Please help me fix this and add a customer support email to your settings.

reviews.title: Wasted Time and Notification Spam
reviews.text:
Edit: Say you don’t want notifications? Well we’re gonna send you quiet ones anyway! What a slimy decision. Respect your users’ choices. 

It’s never a good experience to go through an entire signup process and then pay gate the whole experience. Many other offerings like this have free tiers. It would have been nice to be informed this was a pay-only experience before going through an entire setup and registration process. Be warned to look up pricing and be ready to commit before opening this app.

reviews.title: Learning curve is worth it
reviews.text: My review is based off of a year of use. I also keep to super basic foods so there isn’t much to get wrong. I’m in love with rattling off what I ate and the app doing all the work. Once I learned how to alter foods and save them as faves, it’s been such a luxury. I also enjoy the recap showing water, activity (would love a search feature here) and my progress given in a percentage. The “other” app (you know who I mean) has become clogged with info and options. I like this simpler version. Also on the “other” app, the created foods are overrun with by a million users. As a result me entering chicken inundates me with 1000 versions of the same nutrition panel. I like that this app is still clean. I probably wouldn’t pay more than the $20 a year for it but it’s an incredible resource for my weight loss journey!

reviews.title: Weight Loss Made Simple
reviews.text:
This app is ideal for those who have tried every fad diet or weight loss/food tracking app only to find themselves back at the start of their journey over and over again. 

ParrotPal teaches you how to remove old philosophies and concepts about what it takes to be successful in reaching your weight loss goals by teaching you how to truly live a normal lifestyle and still improve your health. 

I enjoy the ease, flexibility, and convenience of its tracking tools. Additionally, I appreciate the community support they provide on various social media platforms. Continuing to use this app is a must for me. If you decide to try it, I’m sure the same will be true for you.

reviews.title: Disingenuous Bait & switch
reviews.text: F these guys, just another app that mines your personal details and sends you through 30 minutes of setup just to paywall EVERYTHING. They’re BANKING on you feeling pressure from “sunk time” caving and signing up for the free trial subscription. This is so deceptive.

reviews.title: SO EASY…but calories are not always accurate
reviews.text: This app is incredibly easy to use and really reduces the burden of tracking. The barcode scanner, speech to text, it’s all amazing. Lately tho I’ve noticed that some of the calories are quite off. If 1 c milk has 45 cals, 1 tbsp cannot have 35. Some features I’d love to see: ability to set a target goal date, easier account navigation (I’m frequently searching for my settings like my activity level, height and weight but can’t find these anywhere). What happens if someone becomes pregnant-there’s no way to change that detail. There’s also no way to reset your data (deleting the app doesn’t seem to work).

reviews.title: Useful for tracking calories
reviews.text: I like using this to estimate calories or just to log my meals quickly and see my current count. It’s not perfect, sometimes it gets confused when I directly tell it the amount of calories and food item - doubles or changes calories sometimes. Imagine it is conflicting with its database. Also sometimes it logs my calories as 0 and I have to manually change the number. Otherwise good 90% of the time, and keeps me motivated.

reviews.title: Get rid of leanshield
reviews.text: The actual app is great, leanshield is not. Give me back the data button at the bottom and get rid of leanshield. Also keep the metrics consistent either Ibs or Kg but it’s annoying when your app is split 50/50.

reviews.title: Worth it!!
reviews.text: Just finished my 7 day trial and immediately signed up for the year. Scott makes it easy to log my food, not a chore like other trackers do. And if you want macros, the app tells you what they are. Love that I can scan a barcode, take a picture of the food on my plate, or even just voice note my daily meals into the app. And Scott’s accent is divine!! Highly recommend this app!

reviews.title: Annoying onboarding
reviews.text: First you make me answer a huge questionnaire on instagram then once I accept a plan and download the app I have to do it all again.. these deceptive practices are super annoying and turned me off before I even started. I spent like 10 minutes onboarding and then you wanted me to spend another ten.. so necessary… these deceptive practices mid way thru onboarding you say “we have some bad news”… way to engage your audience… terrible user experience and I found all the dialog boxes extremely condescending. Unfortunately that prevented me from using the app. If you’re annoying during onboarding I already know I’m not going to like your product. Hire a good UX designer.

reviews.title: DO NOT PURCHASE
reviews.text: I purchased the year to use it ($39.99). The app is HIGHLY inaccurate. I tried several items, starting with a protein bar - the protein of which is 35g. The app, no matter how I said the bar's name and information, kept telling me it contained only 6g of protein. After several attempts with other foods, I couldn't believe this was a real tracker because it was always wrong against the actual nutritional facts LOL. The best part - I contacted the company for a refund, and "Scott" walked me through the steps to get Apple to refund me (i.e. report a problem, what to say, etc.). Apple denied it. Ball's in your court, Scott, still waiting on you to do something. Oh - FYI, in the email he admits in response that the app has glitches and is nto always right LOL WHAT?!

reviews.title: Made up numbers
reviews.text: The reviews on this app have to be fake. Nothing on this app is remotely accurate. We’ll start with it telling me I need to eat 2,589 calories to lose weight… I’m 5’9” sedentary. That’s about 1,000 calories over what I need to lose weight. Second, NONE of the food calories are accurate. I let it calculate everything throughout the day and it didn’t seem right, so I went and calculated everything manually and EVERY piece of food was off by a ton. I’m talking 70 vs 200 off. This app is complete trash and needs to be pulled from the App Store before it does someone harm. Absolutely ridiculous.

reviews.title: Amazing concept, needs some tweaks
reviews.text: I love this app. I used struggle with logging my food because some days I would be on the move and not have a moment to stop and scan or scroll through items to enter new foods. The voice AI option is fantastic. I can just tell the app which foods I’m eating and it will decipher it (usually with good accuracy) and log my macros. The one thing I have noticed is that when using the voice feature, it doesn’t always log the same macros for the same foods. Calories can vary pretty significantly +/- 10-50cal which is a lot if you’re on a deficit. Use with that in mind. Otherwise, I think it’s great and can’t wait to see what improvements come in the future!

reviews.title: Simple & Sensible
reviews.text:
I’ve used just about all the fitness tracking apps. They’re fine and for someone like me who likes to get analytical with what’s going on with what I eat and do, it’s fun. For a few weeks…and then it just gets unsustainable (I mean…IF I plan to do anything else in my life). ParrotPal is simple to use and the short lessons from Scott Flear are sensible…when you listen you realize 1. You don’t need to make it hard on yourself; 2. Perfection shouldn’t be the goal…progress should be. (Not to mention I dig the accent!)

There are some things that could be better…it would be great if, when you create a recipe, it would ask if you want to “save”or “save and log”. It doesn’t currently allow you to see the measurements entered but am told this will be available soon. 

All in all…I’m loving the app. The apps creator is extremely responsive to users’ questions/comments/concerns via the group messenger and WhatsApp, which is helpful; you don’t feel on your own. It’s simple and the lessons along with the app give you sensible tools for weight loss.

reviews.title: Life changing simplicity
reviews.text:
I’ve lost 10 lbs in just 11 weeks using Parrot Pal, and I’ve never felt overwhelmed by the process. This app finally made tracking sustainable for me.

The ability to snap a photo of my food, scan nutritional labels, and barcodes makes logging fast and stress-free even on busy days. I just focus on three simple things: calories, protein, and movement. That alone has made all the difference, especially since I’d used other trackers before and never saw results.

What sets Parrot Pal apart even more are the daily podcast episodes. They’re short, insightful, and incredibly motivating, like having a coach in your pocket. They help me reset and stay focused, especially when I’m tempted to give up.

If you’re looking for an approach that’s actually doable and gets real results, this is it.

reviews.title: Awesome Calorie Counter
reviews.text: I absolutely love the ease of keeping track of my calories and protein. The best part though are the “real” podcasts. If I crew up Scott is there to tell us to chill, start again and don’t be so hard on ourselves. I love that he says it’s not a diet!

reviews.title: Amazing

I struggle with ADHD and have tried MyFitnessPal and I found it much too busy and confusing with so many different features and add on charges. I love how parrot pal has a basic function and a widget. I was actually able to remember to add in all my foods over the 7 days and usually I’m over MFP by day 1! Great app, wonderful.

reviews.title: Best tracking app ever

Even the AI photo feature is quite accurate. Just makes my life so much easier I don’t have to think about having to manually track everything I eat now.
